description: Tonnes, cubic metres, truck loads and the number of compaction lifts for a Granular A or Granular B base, using the 150 mm lift limit in Toronto standard specification TS 501. Every parameter is optional and has a default. Preliminary planning only. The project specification, the geotechnical report and your supplier's weights govern. The default weight per cubic metre is a general federal stone conversion, not a Granular A or Granular B test result.

allowance.description: Extra material for compaction loss, uneven subgrade and waste. Set it from your supplier or engineer; the default is 0. Unit: percent.

density.description: Weight per cubic metre used to convert volume to tonnes. The default is the federal stone conversion of 1.77 tonnes per cubic metre. Use your supplier's figure when you have it. Unit: kg/m3.

depth.description: Finished (compacted) depth of the granular layer. Unit: mm or in.

length.description: Length of the area. Unit: m or ft.

material.description: Granular A (base course) or Granular B (subbase), as named in OPSS.MUNI 1010.

truck.description: Payload of one truck load. 18 is an example; enter your hauler's figure. Unit: tonnes.

width.description: Width of the area. Unit: m or ft.
